Build the page as one HTML file named index.html in the current directory, with Taproot's web components. There is no bundler: load what the page needs from node_modules. Write the components as markup in the HTML, not from script. When the file is written, reply with one line saying so.

The design system spec holds records: components, patterns, guidelines, and examples. A component
is a technology-neutral contract (anatomy, parameters, states, rules, tokens), not framework code.
Implement it in whatever technology the project uses.

- Use the `taproot` CLI when you have a terminal, and the `taproot` MCP server when you
  do not. Run the CLI from an installed copy, never an `npx` download per call: in this repository,
  `node packages/spec/bin/taproot.js`; in a project that depends on the package,
  `node_modules/.bin/taproot`.
- Start with `search` to choose a component, then `get` it and follow its links: `alternative` for
  when it is the wrong choice, `follows` for the patterns and guidelines it applies, `examples` for
  worked usage.
- Use `rules` to review work, and cite each rule by its address (for example
  `component.button#label-describes-result`) with its level (MUST, SHOULD, MAY). A component's
  rules include those of the patterns and guidelines it follows, at their own addresses (for
  example `pattern.form-field#error-blocks-submit`).
- Use `tokens` for the design tokens a component part uses in a variant or state. Add `--resolve`
  (MCP: `resolve`) for values. Use `format` for what records do not repeat: the system-wide
  constants, such as border width and focus-ring width and offset, with their tokens.
- Before writing code, `get` the component with the implementation for your technology:
  `--impl web` for web components, `--impl react` for React (MCP: `implementation`). It gives the
  package, what to import, and the attribute or prop that implements each parameter. Never derive
  those names from parameter names. Once per project, read `setup --impl <name>` (MCP: `setup`)
  for what every component shares: installing the package, loading its styles, and fonts.
- Components style only themselves. Before building a page, `get guideline.page-setup` for the
  page's base font, text color, background, and heading recipes, and load the base stylesheet it
  names when your technology has one.
- For several lookups, run them in one `batch` with the CLI (for example
  `taproot batch --command "get button --impl web" --command "tokens button"`), or make the
  tool calls in parallel on the MCP server.

content:
# Web components setup

What every web component needs, once per project. Each component's own file in this folder maps its
API; `taproot setup --impl web` prints this one.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @taproot-ds/web-components @taproot-ds/tokens
```

## Load the styles

Load the token stylesheet once, at the application root, before any component renders. Without it,
the components have no colors, spacing, or type. The optional base stylesheet styles the page
around them: the base font, text color, background, and a type recipe for each heading level
(`guideline.page-setup`). The components style only themselves.

```js
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/css";
import "@taproot-ds/tokens/base"; // optional page defaults
```

Without a bundler, link the files from the tokens package instead:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/tokens.css" />
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/node_modules/@taproot-ds/tokens/dist/css/base.css" />
```

The components read semantic tokens directly, so they follow the active theme. With no
`data-theme` on the root element, the theme follows the system preference; `data-theme="light"` or
`"dark"` overrides it. The tokens a component reads are not a customization API.

## Fonts

The font tokens name Lora, Source Sans 3, and JetBrains Mono, with system fallbacks. The packages do
not ship the font files. The tokens package's readme has the links to load them.

## Register the elements

Import the package root once to register every element under its `ds-` tag:

```js
import "@taproot-ds/web-components";
```

Or import one component's module and call its define function, as each component's Import section
shows. A define function takes another tag name when `ds-` names collide.

The modules are standard ES modules with no runtime dependencies. Without a bundler, map the bare
package names with an import map, or import the files under `node_modules/@taproot-ds/web-components/src/`.

content:
# Page setup

Set the page's base font, text color, background, and heading type from semantic tokens, because components style only themselves.

The components style only themselves. The page around them, the text between them, and the
headings above them get no style from any component. Without these defaults, components look right
while the page around them falls back to the platform's serif font and plain white, and nothing
reports the gap.

## What the page sets

| Page element | Token | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Background | `semantic.color.background.default` | The page itself. Raised areas use `semantic.color.background.surface`. |
| Base text | `semantic.typography.body.md` | Font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing. |
| Text color | `semantic.color.foreground.default` | Supporting text uses `semantic.color.foreground.muted`. |
| Small print | `semantic.typography.body.sm` | Captions and fine print. |
| Page title (level 1) | `semantic.typography.heading.lg` | One per page. |
| Section heading (level 2) | `semantic.typography.heading.md` | |
| Subsection heading (level 3) | `semantic.typography.heading.sm` | The recipe Card uses for its title. |
| Deeper headings (levels 4 to 6) | `semantic.typography.title` | The bold sans title Alert and Dialog use. |
| Code | `semantic.typography.code.md` | Inline code and code blocks. |
| Eyebrow above a heading | `semantic.typography.eyebrow` | A short category line, not a heading. |

A typography token such as `semantic.typography.body.md` is a recipe: it groups a font family,
size, weight, line height, and letter spacing, and each is its own token
(`semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily`). Set all five together. Mixing parts of two recipes
produces a size and line height that were never designed together.

For the values in each theme, read the token package, or resolve a component that uses the
recipe, such as `taproot tokens card --part title --resolve`.

## Token names in your technology

A token reference such as `semantic.typography.body.md.fontFamily` is technology-neutral. Each
technology's token package publishes it under its own name, and that package says how. In the web
package, a reference becomes a CSS custom property: prefix `--ds-`, join the segments with hyphens,
and turn camel case into hyphenated words, so the reference above is
`--ds-semantic-typography-body-md-font-family`. Check a name against the package's stylesheet
before you rely on it (`no-guessed-names`).

## Fonts

The font tokens name the system's typefaces with fallbacks. The token package does not ship the
font files. Load the typefaces the way your platform does, before the page renders; the token
package's readme lists them and gives the web links to load them. Without them, the fallbacks keep the page readable but it does not
look like the system.

## Theme

The token package follows the reader's light or dark preference, and lets the page choose one
instead. Set the theme at the root of the page so the background, the base text, and every
component change together. A part of the page that sets its own colors without semantic tokens
does not change with them.

## Spacing and layout

Lay out the page with the spacing primitives, `primitives.space.*`, and put product layout
between components rather than inside them (`guideline.compose-or-propose`). The system has no
grid, container, or page template component; compose those in product code.

## Rules

### Behavior

- **MUST** load-tokens: Load the token package once, at the root of the page, before any component renders. Without it, components have no colors, spacing, or type.
- **MUST** page-base-text: The page's base text uses the body recipe, `semantic.typography.body.md`, in `semantic.color.foreground.default`. Text the components do not draw would otherwise fall back to the platform's default font and color.
- **MUST** page-background: The page background is `semantic.color.background.default`, so it follows the active theme with the components on it.
- **SHOULD** heading-recipes: Each heading level uses a heading recipe: the page title `semantic.typography.heading.lg`, section headings `semantic.typography.heading.md`, subsection headings `semantic.typography.heading.sm`, and deeper levels `semantic.typography.title`. Choose the level by the document outline, and the recipe by the level.
- **SHOULD** base-stylesheet: Where the token package offers a base stylesheet for your technology, load it rather than writing the page defaults by hand. It applies these rules with names that are already right. `taproot setup --impl <name>` names it for each implementation.
- **MUST** no-guessed-names: Take each token's name in your technology from the token package or a lookup, never from a guess. A misspelled token name fails silently and the platform default shows instead.

## Links

### related

- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)

# Text field

Use Text field to collect a single line of text with a label, hint, and error.

Collects one line of text and associates a label, optional hint, and optional error with the control.

## When to use

- Collect a short value such as a name, email, or search query.
- Pair with Button when the value should be submitted.

## When not to use

- Collect multi-line text. Use [Text area](component.text-area) instead. Text field is a single line.
- Choose from a known set of options. Use [Select](component.select) instead. Text field does not present choices.
- Trigger an action by itself. Use [Button](component.button) instead. Text field collects a value.

## Anatomy

| Part | Role | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| field | container | Label, control, hint, and error stacked together. |
| label | label | Visible name for the value. |
| control | interactive-surface | Single-line text control. |
| hint | description | Optional supporting guidance. |
| error | description | Optional message that says what to fix. |

## Parameters

| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| hint | string |  |  | Supporting guidance. Included in the accessible description when set. |

215	# Dialog
216	
217	Use Dialog for a focused task or confirmation that temporarily blocks the surrounding view.
218	
219	Presents a named modal conversation above the current view. Focus stays inside until the dialog closes, then returns to the person’s previous position in the workflow.
220	
221	## When to use
222	
223	- Confirm a consequential action with explicit action and cancel choices.
224	- Complete a short task without leaving the current view.
225	
226	## When not to use
227	
228	- Show a passive status message that needs no response. Use [Alert](component.alert) instead. Blocking the view interrupts the person unnecessarily.
229	- Present a long workflow or primary page content. Instead: A dedicated view. Long tasks need room and a persistent location.

286	- **MUST** visible-title: Supply a visible title that names the task or decision.
287	- **SHOULD** action-emphasis: Assign emphasis to actions by consequence and importance.
288	  - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis
289	
290	### Behavior
291	
292	- **MUST** explicit-exit: Provide an explicit cancel or close action, including when standard dismissal is disabled.
293	- **MUST** modal-background: While open, prevent interaction with the surrounding view.
294	- **MUST** cancellation: An unhandled Escape or standard platform cancel gesture requests dismissal only when dismissible is true. Preventing the cancel event leaves the dialog open. Controls within the dialog may consume Escape for their own interaction, and Escape during text composition does not request dismissal. Dismissal affects only the active modal conversation. Clicking the backdrop never closes the dialog.
295	- **MUST** close-notification: Report close once after each open dialog closes. Closing an already closed dialog does nothing.
296	- **MUST** content-scroll: Keep the dialog within the available viewport, allow overflowing dialog content to scroll, and prevent scrolling the surrounding view while open.
297	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
298	  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.
299	
300	### Accessibility
301	
302	- **MUST** initial-focus: Move focus inside on opening. Focus the title by default so opening cannot accidentally activate a destructive choice. Consumers may designate a suitable control for initial focus.
303	- **MUST** contain-focus: Forward and reverse sequential focus navigation stay within the open dialog.
304	- **MUST** restore-focus: On close, return focus to the element that had it before opening if that element still exists and can receive focus. Otherwise the consumer chooses a logical next workflow position.
305	- **MUST** accessible-modal: Expose dialog role, modal state, title, and any supplied description to assistive technology.
306	- **MUST** visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated, including when the title receives initial focus.
307	  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#visible-focus
308	  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
309	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#forced-colors: Under forced colors, every boundary, indicator, and focus ring that carries meaning stays visible, and each state stays distinguishable without the theme's colors.
310	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.
311	
312	## Accessibility
313	
314	- Role: Dialog
315	- Name: Required from its visible title.
316	
317	| Key | Action |
318	| --- | --- |
319	| Tab | Move to the next focusable item within the open dialog. |
320	| Shift+Tab | Move to the previous focusable item within the open dialog. |
321	| Escape | Request dismissal when dismissible; cancellation can be prevented. |
322	
323	## Rationale
324	
325	- **The label and description are options of the title and description parts. Open and dismissible stay options of the dialog.** Each of the first two fills one part (ADR 0005). The dialog takes its accessible name and description from those parts. Open and dismissible govern the whole modal conversation.
326	- **Modal only, one responsive size, no density variant, and no nested dialogs.** This first contract serves short focused tasks. Dialog width is bounded by the viewport; consumers needing long tasks use a dedicated view. Non-modal panels and nested conversations introduce different focus and interaction requirements.
327	- **No disabled, selected, checked, invalid, loading, or icon-only state.** These states belong to composed controls and actions. Dialog always has a visible title; waiting for work must still provide a usable exit or explain how to cancel.
328	- **Actions and close controls are composed with Button.** Dialog owns modal behavior, while consumers own action labels and task outcomes.
329	- **No backdrop dismissal and no opening or closing animation.** A stray pointer action should not discard a task. Instant transitions also satisfy reduced motion preferences without a separate motion treatment.
330	- **Layout follows reading direction; no directional artwork.** Title, content, and actions follow the surrounding right-to-left or left-to-right flow.
331	- **Semantic surface and overlay roles, with spacing primitives.** Semantic tokens cover surface, foreground, border, radius, elevation, and the backdrop. The overlay role is darker in the dark theme, where the same scrim as in light dims the page less. Spacing primitives describe this surface’s padding and gaps. The title uses semantic.typography.title, as in Alert.
332	
333	## Links
334	
335	### alternative
336	
337	- [Alert](component.alert) — Show a passive status message that needs no response. Blocking the view interrupts the person unnecessarily.
338	
339	### alternative-to
340	
341	- [Accordion](component.accordion) — A focused task that should block the rest of the view until it is done. An accordion section opens in place and blocks nothing.
342	- [Alert](component.alert) — Ask for a decision before the person can continue. Alert does not block the view or hold focus. Dialog does.
343	- [Card](component.card) — Ask for a decision or hold a task that blocks the rest of the view. Dialog holds focus until the task ends. A card sits in the flow of the page.
344	- [Tooltip](component.tooltip) — Show content that has links, buttons, or more than a short phrase. A tooltip cannot be interacted with and disappears when the pointer leaves. Content a person has to read or act on needs a surface they open on purpose.
345

348	- [Button](component.button)

350	### follows
351	
352	- [Accessibility](guideline.accessibility)
353	- [Compose or propose](guideline.compose-or-propose)
354	- [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy)
355	- [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis)

357	## Web implementation
358	
359	- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
360	- Element: `<ds-dialog>`
361	
362	### Import
363	
364	```js
365	import { defineDialog } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/dialog";
366	
367	defineDialog();
368	```
369	
370	### Usage
371	
372	```html
373	<ds-dialog label="Delete project?" description="This cannot be undone.">
374	  <p>Delete the archived project and its files.</p>
375	  <ds-button slot="actions" variant="secondary">Cancel</ds-button>
376	  <ds-button slot="actions" variant="destructive">Delete project</ds-button>
377	</ds-dialog>
378	```
379	
380	### API
381	
382	| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
383	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
384	| `open` | attribute | parameter `open` | boolean | Whether the modal dialog is shown. |
385	| `dismissible` | attribute | parameter `dismissible` | boolean | Whether the standard cancel gesture can request dismissal. |
386	| `showModal` | property |  | `() => void` | Sets open to true and opens the connected dialog modally. |
387	| `close` | property |  | `() => void` | Sets open to false and closes the dialog. |
388	| `cancel` | event | event `cancel` |  | A cancel gesture requests dismissal; the consumer may prevent it to protect unfinished work. |
389	| `close` | event | event `close` |  | The dialog has closed, through an explicit action, dismissal, or programmatic change. |
390	
391	A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.
392	
393	### Title part, on `<ds-dialog>`
394	
395	| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
396	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
397	| `label` | attribute | title parameter `label` | string | Visible title and accessible name for the dialog. |
398	
399	### Description part, on `<ds-dialog>`
400	
401	| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
402	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
403	| `description` | attribute | description parameter `description` | string | Optional short accessible description of the conversation. |
404	
405	### Open and close
406	
407	Call `showModal()` on the host or set its `open` property. Both use native `dialog.showModal()`
408	inside the shadow root. Call `close()` from each composed cancel or completion button. Content
409	uses the default slot; action buttons use `slot="actions"`. Consumer actions do not close automatically.
410	
411	`dismissible` defaults to true. Set the property to false or use `dismissible="false"` to block
412	Escape. A permitted Escape sends a cancelable `cancel` event from the host; call `preventDefault()`
413	to retain unfinished work. Listen for `close` to synchronize application state.
414	
415	### Focus and lifecycle
416	
417	The visible title receives initial focus. Set `autofocus` on a suitable slotted control to choose it
418	instead. Open dialogs keep Tab and Shift+Tab within composed controls, including open shadow roots.
419	Closing restores focus to the prior control if it still exists. If the opener was removed, focus the
420	next workflow control from your close listener.
421	
422	Hiding or disconnecting an open host releases its scroll lock and reports close. The `open` request
423	remains set when hidden, so unhiding reopens it. In controlled frameworks, clear application open
424	state on close when hiding should permanently dismiss the task.
425	
426	The component uses native modal background blocking and a document scroll lock. It restores the
427	previous inline overflow value and priority when the final dialog lock closes. Keep dialogs at the
428	application level and avoid placing them inside inert or hidden ancestors.
429	
430	The internal native dialog uses `closedby="closerequest"` when dismissible, preserving platform
431	close requests such as the system back gesture. When dismissal is disabled it uses
432	`closedby="none"`. Native cancel requests still pass through the host's cancelable `cancel` event.
433	
434	Unconsumed Escape is handled in the bubble phase for the active dialog, including when focus has
435	fallen back to the document body. A child control must call `preventDefault()` to consume Escape
436	without dismissing the dialog; `stopPropagation()` alone does not prevent a native close request.
437	Composing key events do not request dismissal through the component keyboard handler.
438

440	Setup: install, styles, and fonts are the same for every component. Run `taproot setup --impl web` once per project.

444	# Button
445	
446	Use Button to trigger an action or to submit or reset a form.
447	
448	Triggers an action or submits or resets a form.
449	
450	## When to use
451	
452	- Trigger an action in the current view.
453	- Submit or reset a form.
454	
455	## When not to use
456	
457	- Navigate to another location. Use [Link](component.link) instead. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.
458	- Display status or metadata. Use [Badge](component.badge) instead. Button communicates an available action.
459	
460	## Anatomy
461	
462	| Part | Role | Description |
463	| --- | --- | --- |
464	| control | interactive-surface | Interactive control. |
465	| content | label | Action label with an optional decorative icon. |
466	
467	## Parameters
468	
469	| Name | Kind | Values | Default | Description |
470	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
471	| variant | enum | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` | `primary` |  |
472	| size | enum | `small`, `medium` | `medium` |  |
473	| action | enum | `activate`, `submit`, `reset` | `activate` |  |
474	| disabled | boolean |  | `false` |  |
475	| fullWidth | boolean |  | `false` | Fills the available inline size. |
476	| accessibleName | string |  |  | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. |
477	
478	`variant` values:
479	
480	- `primary`: Highest-emphasis action. Example: Save changes Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#primary)
481	- `secondary`: Supporting action. Example: Cancel Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#secondary)
482	- `tertiary`: Low-emphasis action. Example: View details Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#tertiary)
483	- `destructive`: Destructive or difficult-to-reverse action. Example: Delete project Guidance: [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#destructive)
484	
485	`size` values:
486	
487	- `small`: Small button.
488	- `medium`: Medium button.
489	
490	`action` values:
491	
492	- `activate`: Triggers an action.
493	- `submit`: Submits the associated form.
494	- `reset`: Resets the associated form.
495	
496	## Events
497	
498	- `activate`: Requests the action represented by the button.
499	
500	## States
501	
502	`disabled`, `pressed`, `hover`, `focus`, `default`
503	
504	## Preferences
505	
506	- `reducedMotion`: `reduce`
507	
508	## Rules
509	
510	Includes the rules of guideline.accessibility, which this component follows. Cite each rule by the address shown.
511	
512	### Content
513	
514	- **MUST** label-describes-result: Use a concise label that describes the result.
515	  - Do: Save changes; Delete account
516	  - Avoid: Click here
517	- **MUST** destructive-for-risky-actions: Use the destructive variant only for destructive or difficult-to-reverse actions.
518	- **SHOULD** explain-disabled: When the context does not say why an action is disabled, say why near it.
519	- **SHOULD** follow-action-hierarchy: Apply the action hierarchy pattern when several actions appear together.
520	  - See: pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis
521	
522	### Behavior
523	
524	- **MUST** disabled-prevents-activation: Disabled prevents activation.
525	- **SHOULD** explicit-form-action: In a form, set action to submit or reset when the button should submit or reset. The default activate does neither.
526	- **SHOULD** form-submit-reset: Submit submits the button's form, and reset restores that form's initial values.
527	  - Applies when: The button belongs to a form.
528	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-a-control: The component is not focusable and does not activate.
529	  - Applies when: The component is not interactive.
530	
531	### Accessibility
532	
533	- **MUST** icon-accessible-name: Icon-only buttons have an accessible name.
534	- **MUST** forced-colors: Under forced colors, emphasis stays visible: primary and destructive are filled, secondary is outlined, and tertiary is text alone. A disabled button stays distinguishable from an enabled one.
535	  - Extends: guideline.accessibility#forced-colors
536	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#visible-focus: Keyboard focus is visibly indicated on every focusable part, in every variant and state.
537	  - Applies when: A part of the component takes keyboard focus.
538	- **MUST** guideline.accessibility#not-color-alone: Meaning never depends on color alone. Text, shape, or position carries it too.
539	
540	## Accessibility
541	
542	- Role: Button
543	- Name: Required from visible content or accessibleName.
544	
545	| Key | Action |
546	| --- | --- |
547	| Tab | Move focus to or from the button. |
548	| Enter | Activate. |
549	| Space | Activate. |
550	
551	## Rationale
552	
553	- **Button reads semantic tokens directly and has no component-token namespace.** Its component tokens only restated the semantic tier, so they added names without adding a customization boundary (tokens ADR 0003).
554	
555	## Links
556	
557	### alternative
558	
559	- [Badge](component.badge) — Display status or metadata. Button communicates an available action.
560	- [Link](component.link) — Navigate to another location. A link carries a destination that people can open, copy, or share.
561	
562	### alternative-to
563	
564	- [Avatar](component.avatar) — Open a profile or account menu by pressing the avatar. Avatar is not a control. Place it inside a Button or a Link, which give the action its role, focus, and accessible name.
565	- [Badge](component.badge) — Trigger an action in the current view. Badge is not interactive and does not communicate an available action.
566	- [Card](component.card) — Make a large target that only triggers one action or navigates, with no content of its own. A control styled as a card hides its role. Use Button for an action, or Link for navigation, and let the card hold content.
567	- [Checkbox](component.checkbox) — Trigger an action by itself. Checkbox records a choice.
568	- [Icon](component.icon) — Trigger an action with an icon alone. Icon is not a control. A button with an icon and an accessible name gives the action semantics and focus.
569	- [Link](component.link) — Trigger an action or submit a form. Buttons provide action semantics and form behavior.
570	- [Text field](component.text-field) — Trigger an action by itself. Text field collects a value.

597	## Web implementation
598	
599	- Package: `@taproot-ds/web-components`
600	- Element: `<ds-button>`
601	
602	### Import
603	
604	```js
605	import { defineButton } from "@taproot-ds/web-components/button";
606	
607	defineButton();
608	```
609	
610	### Usage
611	
612	```html
613	<ds-button variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
614	```
615	
616	### API
617	
618	| Name | Kind | Implements | Values | Description |
619	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
620	| `variant` | attribute | parameter `variant` | `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `destructive` |  |
621	| `size` | attribute | parameter `size` | `small`, `medium` |  |
622	| `type` | attribute | parameter `action` | `activate` → `button`, `submit`, `reset` |  |
623	| `disabled` | attribute | parameter `disabled` | boolean |  |
624	| `full-width` | attribute | parameter `fullWidth` | boolean | Fills the available inline size. |
625	| `aria-label` | attribute | parameter `accessibleName` | string | Accessible name when visible content is insufficient. |
626	| `form` | property |  | `HTMLFormElement \| null` | The associated form, including association across the shadow boundary. |
627	| `click` | event | event `activate` |  | Requests the action represented by the button. |
628	
629	A row with no Implements entry is specific to this implementation, not part of the spec.
630	
631	### Forms
632	
633	Button defaults to `type="button"`. Set the type when it participates in a form:
634	
635	```html
636	<form>
637	  <!-- form fields -->
638	  <ds-button type="button" variant="secondary">Cancel</ds-button>
639	  <ds-button type="submit" variant="primary">Save changes</ds-button>
640	</form>
641	```
642	
643	Use `type="reset"` only when restoring every form control to its initial value is the intended
644	behavior.
645	
646	### Styles
647	
648	Do not recreate Button states with product CSS. Use the published variants and sizes first. Treat
649	`::part(button)` as an escape hatch that requires a specific product need and design review.
650	
651	### Icons
652	
653	Mark a decorative icon hidden from assistive technology. Provide `aria-label` when an icon is the
654	only visible content.
655	
656	### Why `aria-label` and not `label`
657	
658	Button maps `accessibleName` to `aria-label`, while Icon, Spinner, and Tabs map it to `label`. The
659	difference is deliberate. `aria-label` is the attribute people already put on an icon-only button,
660	and Button only passes it to the native button inside, so it keeps its standard meaning. The other
661	three use `label` because their name does more than name: Icon is hidden from assistive technology
662	without one, Spinner falls back to "Loading", and Tabs names the tab list inside it rather than the
663	host. They set the name through `ElementInternals` or on that inner element, so the host never
664	gains `aria-*` attributes. Renaming either side would break published markup.

671	# Form field
672	
673	Give every form control the same label, hint, error, required, disabled, and form behavior.
674	
675	Text field, Text area, Select, Checkbox, Switch, Radio group, and Slider follow this pattern and
676	inherit the rules above. Keyboard focus and forced colors come from `guideline.accessibility`,
677	which they also follow. Each keeps only the rules about its own control. It narrows a rule where its
678	control differs, such as what its value is, and waives one that cannot apply, with the reason.
679	
680	## Label, hint, and error
681	
682	The label says what the value is. The hint says what the label cannot, such as a format or a
683	consequence. The error says how to fix what was entered. Assistive technology reads the label as the
684	control's name and the hint and error as its description, so each must make sense on its own.
685	
686	## Switch and forms
687	
688	Switch applies its setting immediately, without a separate submit action. It can also submit with a
689	form, so these rules apply to it. Use Checkbox when the choice takes effect only when the form is
690	submitted.
691	
692	## Rules
693	
694	### Content
695	
696	- **MUST** visible-label: Provide a visible label that names the value. Placeholder text is not a label.
697	  - Do: Email address
698	  - Avoid: Enter email
699	- **SHOULD** hint-adds-information: Use a hint only for format, purpose, or consequence that the label does not already state.
700	- **MUST** error-says-what-to-fix: Write the error as what to fix.
701	  - Do: Enter an email address with an @ sign
702	  - Avoid: Invalid
703	- **SHOULD** explain-disabled: When the reason a control is unavailable is not obvious, explain it nearby.
704	
705	### Behavior
706	
707	- **MUST** error-marks-invalid: A non-empty error marks the control invalid, and clearing the error removes that state.
708	- **SHOULD** clear-error: Clear the error when the person edits the value, and on form reset, which restores the value but leaves the error.
709	- **MUST** error-blocks-submit: While a non-empty error is set, the control blocks its form from submitting.
710	- **MUST** required-blocks-submit: A required control with no value blocks its form from submitting.
711	- **MUST** disabled-prevents-interaction: Disabled prevents interaction from pointer and keyboard.
712	- **MUST** disabled-submits-nothing: A disabled control submits nothing.
713	- **SHOULD** form-value: Inside a form, the control's value submits under its name, and reset restores the initial value.
714	  - Applies when: The control belongs to a form.
715	
716	### Accessibility
717	
718	- **MUST** label-is-name: The visible label is the control's accessible name.
719	- **MUST** described-by-hint-and-error: The hint and the error are associated with the control, so assistive technology reads them as its description.
720	- **MUST** invalid-not-color-alone: The invalid state always includes the error text, so meaning never depends on color alone.
721	- **MUST** required-announced: A required control is announced as required, and shows it by more than color.

$ taproot get example.action-hierarchy.settings
# Settings action hierarchy

A settings screen separates routine profile actions from destructive account deletion.

This account settings screen contains two independent action groups.

The profile form pairs a secondary "Cancel" action with one primary "Save changes" action. The
primary action completes the routine editing task.

Account deletion is destructive and operates on a different subject. A labeled danger zone
separates it from the profile form. Its supporting text explains the consequence before the person
reaches the destructive Button.

![Account settings action hierarchy](assets/action-hierarchy-settings.svg)

## What this example demonstrates

- Hierarchy applies within an action group rather than across the whole page.
- A supporting action remains visible without competing with the primary path.
- A destructive action is separated from routine actions.
- Button labels name their results.
- Text and structure communicate purpose and risk without relying on color.

## What this example does not decide

The example does not define universal button ordering. Products must follow their established
reading direction and platform convention while preserving the semantic hierarchy.

## Annotations

- **Routine action group** (`example.action-hierarchy.settings#profile-actions`): Cancel supports the task and Save changes completes it, so the group uses secondary and primary emphasis. See [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#assign-emphasis).
- **Destructive action group** (`example.action-hierarchy.settings#danger-zone`): Delete account acts on a different subject and is separated into a labeled danger zone. See [Action hierarchy](pattern.action-hierarchy#separate-unrelated-decisions).
- **Outcome-based labels** (`example.action-hierarchy.settings#outcome-labels`): Save changes and Delete account state their results without relying on color. See [Button](component.button#label-describes-result).
